widths.note: 50' west of Spring Grove (this sheet); 60' east of it on sheet 247

bends.note: turns from NNW-SSE (about 15 deg off vertical) to due N-S; both street lines kink (west line at 5224,5700, east line at 5836,5644)

notes: Names printed without a suffix (VALLEY, ALFRED, DRAPER) are written with 'Street'. Valley runs along the west edge next to the binding with a railroad siding in it (centre x~338 at Alfred, ~366 at Queen City; the gutter bends the page slightly). Alfred jogs at Valley: east of Valley it is 60' (lines y~282/651, centre ~466), west of Valley it is only 30' (lines y~301/485, centre ~393, labelled 30' on the gutter side), with the north lines nearly aligned; recorded as two T points, the west piece as 'Alfred Street (west of Valley)'. Draper ends at Valley (T) and crosses Spring Grove (continues east on 247 as a 60' street); the Spring Grove/Draper point is the middle of the open crossing (Draper's centreline is ~20 px higher on the east side, where it is wider). Spring Grove is 100' and bends to due N-S about 1600 px north of Queen City. Buck Street (no width printed, ~40 ft as drawn) leaves Queen City to the south (sheet 234) and is a T. Valley and Spring Grove both continue south of Queen City. Circled figures (62', 64', 65', 66') are grade elevations, not widths. No alleys; the lines in the big blocks are lot lines and a railroad spur (ignored). The east margin (sheet 247) is drawn only to x~4876, so Cook Street is not on this sheet.
